Episode 210. Memories of the Past - Murakan (2)
Murakan was able to open his eyes in the Garden of Swords only a month after the event.
"Sir Murakan is showing signs of awakening!"
"Sir Murakan! Can you hear my voice?"
Diana was the one who rescued the fallen him. If she hadn't arrived in time, Murakan would have drawn his last breath.
"Murakan!"
Diana rushed into the sickroom. Seeing Murakan struggling to sit up as soon as he regained consciousness, Diana screamed in surprise.
"What are you doing, stay still. We had to get the help of the Sagittarius and even brought the Holy King to save you."

"Tamar... I have to stop Tamar. He came to his senses for a moment at the last moment, but I missed because I was weak-hearted. He said he would turn into a monster again, that he had no other choice."
"Stop moving, the wound will open."
"No, no. He was completely back. Yes, he definitely regained his senses. Where is Tamar?"
"Murakan."
"Where is he... Cough."
Murakan hunched over, coughing up a murky energy. Diana carefully laid him back down.
"The Lord is currently with Lord Soldieret at the Storm Castle."
"Ah, of course! That damned guy is okay, right?"
"Yes. So relax and rest. According to the Holy King and the Lord of the Sagittarius, if you walk just five steps now, you will surely die."
Murakan could not receive any essential treatment.

No matter how great the Holy King's divine power, it was impossible to fix the destroyed heart of the black dragon. The Holy King, together with the Lord of Sagittarius, only took minimal measures to prevent the heart from further disintegration.
Either Soldieret directly heals him or he regenerates on his own was the only way to recover.
But Soldieret didn't have much energy left, and it was impossible to know how much time natural healing would take.
'The Holy King said the will of Murakan himself is the most important in self-regeneration. But can Murakan... really want to live?'
The fact that Tamar was with Soldieret at the Storm Castle was true.
But as soon as Tamar was far from Murakan, he immediately went insane, and Soldieret, risking his life, had cast a barrier over the entire area of the Storm Castle.

Diana remembered the words Murakan unconsciously spilled while he was wandering the crossroads of life and death. They were all cries smeared with guilt about the Ten Knights who turned into monsters and Tamar.
There was no one among his colleagues who didn't know how much Murakan loved and cherished them. Diana was barely enduring the sadness.
'Soon, like those who left before, I will become a phantom of manipulation... I am still holding on because they don't know much about me, but eventually, I won't be able to avoid it.'
Before that happens.

She had to carry out the last order left by the Lord before he went mad. She had to leave the spark of the family, hope in the world. She had to prevent the world from completely falling into Ziepel's hands.
While Diana was thinking for a moment, Murakan seemed to fall asleep with difficulty.
When he regained consciousness again, another week had passed.
His whole body was hot like a fireball, and a rough iron sound was made each time he breathed. He couldn't even open his eyes in confusion and vertigo.
Faintly, he heard the voices of those who were guarding his side.
'Diana... and the first-class steward, Kin...'
He couldn't open his mouth. There was almost no sensation throughout his body.
"Kin."
Kin was the first-class steward of Runcandel.
"You wanted to say something... Diana."
"Is the chief steward... not... here?"
"That's correct."
"Could Ziepel have attacked the chief steward at the meeting?"
"It shouldn't be. Even if they did, Sara and Veil would have been able to escape."
His hearing wasn't perfect, so he couldn't hear the entire conversation. It would usually be content easy enough to understand, but even that was difficult for Murakan.
"Ah, Murakan. Close your eyes and rest more."
"Drav... Viol... Fre..."
"They seem to be on a mission. They came to see you a few days ago..."
They had come to see him.
At those words, Murakan unknowingly smiled. Thinking of their faces made his chest hurt momentarily, but the longing and glad feelings were much greater.
Murakan fell asleep again with a smile.
Another month passed.
"Your Majesty, the Holy King, is Murakan getting any better...?"
"According to Ayulra's response, he has no will to live. They say he is content with the fantasies he sees in a comatose state."
"Sigh."
"...... It's a terrible thing. He had to let go of the people he cherished the most with his own hands. I pray that one day he will find his rest."
Every once in a while, when he regained consciousness.
Murakan couldn't properly distinguish between Diana's lies, his imagination, and the harsh reality.
Diana had no choice but to continue lying to him. She could not emphasize the truth to someone who might let go of the faint thread of life at any moment.
"Tamar... Tamar is safe too..."
Every time she heard Murakan's voice, she felt awkward. She didn't have much time left for herself either.
Diana confirmed that Murakan had fallen asleep again and sought the Storm Castle. The darkened barrier of Soldelet wrapped around the Storm Castle.
Even though Ziepel knew that Soldelet was not complete, he had never attacked Storm Castle since he set up the barrier.
As Diana approached, the barrier opened for a moment. Inside the castle, Silderei and the knights greeted her.
"Diana."
"Silderei, how is the Lord?"
"He's the same. He became a ghost, then returned to his original form briefly, then lost consciousness."
That was why Silderei and the knights were waiting at the Storm Castle. They needed people to suppress Tamar when he raged, not kill him.
Silderei had already suppressed Tamar dozens of times. He, too, was barely enduring his inner exhaustion.
"What about Murakan?"
"The Holy King received a response from Ayulra about Murakan, and it's not good."
"I see……"
Currently, Runcandel was waiting for a response to the surrender proposed by Loret, delivered to Ziepel last time.
"When the Lord returns to his original form once in a while, does he leave any special words?"
"The words he left when he first came to Storm Castle were his last."
"I see."
"Diana. If Ziepel refuses the surrender, what happens to us?"
"We have to fight to the death."
That was not scary at all.

What was frightening was to become their puppet without even being able to fight due to manipulation. To unknowingly kill people like the comrades who had died to Murakan. Dying in battle was, at best, a hopeful scenario.

"Honestly, I don't understand. They have no reason to accept the surrender. It's better to disappear after fighting with all your might while your mind is still intact. We shouldn't be this cowardly!"
As Silderei said, it didn't seem like there was a particular reason for Ziepel to accept the surrender.
In the war, Runcandel eventually suffered irreparable damage, while Ziepel, with Elona Ziepel intact, had almost completed the method of history manipulation.
If Runcandel just waited like this, it would soon be destroyed. Either it would become a ghost of history manipulation, or it would be brutally killed by the magicians.
Silderei thought that Ziepel was not attacking the Storm Castle and the Garden of the Sword now because they didn't need to waste their forces.
In the history of Ziepel, which has ruled the world for more than two thousand years, Runcandel was the only counterforce.
Ziepel had no reason to leave a spark of such Runcandel. Ziepel's way was to erase everything related to Runcandel, even a small pebble, from the world.
Diana did not answer and headed towards Tamar's sickbed. And she sat quietly for several hours, watching him.
During this, she saw Tamar slowly get up and start turning into a purple hue.
"Ha."
"Diana and Silderei were able to subdue the rampaging Temar without difficulty. Just as Murakan's heart was broken, Temar was also weakened due to the fight with him.
Temar lost consciousness as soon as he was subdued and returned to his original form.
Diana stepped outside to cool her head and lit a cigarette, while Silderei leaned against Temar's bed and burst into tears.
"Everyone's master... Damn! Solderet, this damn traitor! Is this what you meant by keeping your promise! Come out, show yourself, you damned...!"
As Silderei howled, a group of knights who had been outside hurriedly entered the sickroom. They tried to restrain Silderei, but they could not overcome his great strength.
"Silderei! If you act like this, what are the other knights supposed to do? Calm down, please!"
"It wasn't the Guardian who made the master like this. Lower your voice, Silderei."
"Who else but Solderet made the master like this? When the master was afflicted, where was that useless god and what was he doing?"
"What blasphemy are you spouting, Silderei?"
Diana returned to the bedside and grabbed Silderei's shoulder.
"Blasphemy?"
"Didn't you hear the master's last command? Do not resent the Guardian, fulfill the promise you made with the Guardian. Even while losing consciousness, he urged us several times."
The promise.
The promise Solderet made with Lunakandel was survival. It was about preparing for a thousand years later.
"Diana, do you still trust Solderet after seeing the master in this state...?"
"Whether I trust or not is not the important issue."
"Look at this, you no longer trust Solderet either, right? You feel the same as me, Diana. Don't I know you?"

"My feelings are also not important. Silderei, what's important is... that it's the master's command. The master's command is absolute, it's us who made the law of Lunakandel! If you continue to show this ugly side, even if it's you, I will not let it slide."
"Hah."
"Accept the master's command. The only obligation and hope left for us is that alone."

"What kind of hope is this, waiting for them to accept our surrender! A thousand years? Was everything we've done so far for the contractor of a thousand years later? Solderet knew this would happen from the beginning. He only used the master and us."
Diana held Silderei in her arms for a while as he vented his anger.

She didn't disagree with Silderei's words either. However, because the master's command is absolute, she was just following it. If that was the only means to defeat their enemies someday, even if late, they had to follow it.

"Solderet said he would use our souls to create guardians. Is he trying to protect Lunakandel through those guardians, even if we become monsters...? But even if that guardian has the same power as us, it won't be able to stop Elona and Ziffle."
Suddenly, urgent footsteps were heard in the hallway.
"Silderei, Diana! Ziffle's response has arrived."
